text:
maria: Heads-up from QA — the structured-output validation banner reads "Schema mismatch" and folks keep opening support tickets because they don't know what went wrong.
kevin: Yeah that wording is too terse. For integrators we should show what failed and next steps. Suggest short banner + expandable details.
sam: Two scenarios: 1) parser couldn't deserialize (bad JSON), 2) payload passed JSON but failed schema validation (missing/invalid fields). Wording should guide both.
jane: Accessibility nit: banners must be role=alert and keyboard-focusable for keyboard users. Expandable details should be a collapse region with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
ui-bot: Accessibility checklist: role=alert, aria-live polite for non-blocking notices, expand/collapse buttons keyboard accessible, don't rely on color alone to indicate severity. Keep primary message <= 80 chars.
kevin: Draft microcopy (banner compact):
```
Structured output validation failed — some fields didn't match the expected schema. Show details
```
kevin: Expand details modal (short):
```
Title: Validation details
Body: The model response could not be used because one or more fields failed validation. Example: "user.age" expected integer but got ""27"". This may be due to model hallucination or prompt mismatch.
What you can do:
• Check your schema and example prompts
• Enable "Show raw response" to inspect the full output
• Retry the request or fallback to a text-only response
Link: Read more about structured output validation
```
sam: For the compact banner prefer the verb "failed" over "mismatch". Also include an unobtrusive error code in the details: VALIDATION_SCHEMA_400. Support can triage faster.
maria: Tone: avoid blaming the model. Use neutral guidance like "This may be due to model output or prompt shape." Keep the first line action-oriented: "Validation failed — check details."
jane: For screen readers expand the example inline in the details region. Use preformatted text for the snippet and ensure contrast. Also ensure the "Show raw response" toggle is announced when opened.
kevin: UX behavior: banner shows for errors that occur synchronously. For background validation failures (async) surface a toast and link to the request log. The details view should include a copyable snippet and a "Create support ticket" CTA prefilled with the validation error summary.
maria: Nice. Can devs implement: new banner copy, details modal, error code field, and analytics event when users view details? I'll do a final copy pass when the mock is up.
kevin: I'll update the component and push a screenshot to #design in 30m. :mag:
